newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Burundi's Hutu rebel group condemns hangings.
newsitem.headline: Burundi's Hutu rebel group condemns hangings.

text.p: Burundi's Hutu rebel group on Sunday condemned the execution of six people in the capital Bujumbura and warned the government it may pull out of talks to end the country's civil war.

The National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD) said the hangings carried out in Bujumbura's central prison on Thursday violated an agreement signed in Rome in March with the Burundi government on future peace negotiations.

The accord called for the creation of an international crime tribunal to judge acts of genocide and other political crimes committed in Burundi, a former Belgian colony. The trials of the six men were carried by the local judicial authorities.
"If (Burundi's military ruler Pierre) Buyoya continues with his policy of violating the accord we will have to reconsider the talks," CNDD's spokesman Jerome Ndiho told Reuters.
CNDD, which has been fighting the Tutsi-led army for a greater political stake in the country, also alleged that five out of the six hung were Hutus.
Burundi's ministry of justice has said the men were three Hutus, two Tutsis and one ethnic Twa.
"The CNDD condemns the execution at the Mpimba maximum prison of five Hutu and one of the intellectuals of the ethnic group Twa," CNDD said in a statement.
More than 150,000 people have died in ethnic violence since 1993 after soldiers from the Tutsi-dominated army assassinated the country's first freely-elected president, Melchior Ndadaye, a Hutu.
The United States on Friday condemned the hangings and called on the government to halt all executions and suspend all trials related to the assassination of Ndadaye.
The international human rights group Amnesty International also criticised the executions, saying they took place after "blatantly unfair trials".
